brief: Deutsche Bank's week-ahead note argues that Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI may determine whether the Fed hikes at the September 16 FOMC meeting. August payrolls rose 162k with 55k of upward revisions, private payrolls rose 127k, and the 3- and 6-month averages moved to +75k and +106k, with the six-month diffusion rate at 55.8. Unemployment ticked up to 4.14% while U-6 fell to 7.7% and participation rose to 61.6%, though that rise mostly reversed July declines and prime-age participation held at 85.4%. DB reads this as a broadly stable labor market with a 0-50k monthly breakeven and possible early signs that gains exceed it. Chair Warsh's focus on prices and Waller's remark that hot inflation could support a September 16 hike raise the weight on this week's prints. DB forecasts headline CPI +0.38% on a 4.4% seasonally adjusted gas price rise, core +0.21%, and an implied core PCE of +0.21%, which would leave core PCE at 3.3% year over year. A 21bp implied core PCE would lean toward a hike without automatically triggering one. DB concludes a September hike is the most likely outcome absent a meaningful downside surprise.
